previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, autonomic dysfunction, and coronary artery disease was admitted for chest pressure, hypertension, and generalized weakness. His symptoms began over the weekend with elevated blood pressure and headache, which partially improved with rest. He presented to his primary care provider with new-onset chest pressure, nausea, and reduced oral intake. Evaluation revealed no acute cardiac ischemia, with normal EKG and undetectable troponin. A chest X-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. He was treated with IV fluids, leading to resolution of chest pressure and improvement in orthostatic symptoms. His outpatient cardiologist, neurologist, and mitochondrial specialist were consulted; no new therapies were recommended due to his initial hypertension. Outpatient IV hydration was arranged closer to his home. He was discharged asymptomatic with continued management focused on hydration and monitoring.

disease requiring regular IVF infusions, CAD, htn, HL who

#1 and tolerated the infusion well with only mild hypertension.  
However, on hospital day #2, he developed chest pressure, 
shortness of breath, hypertension and a feeling of being ill.  
His chest pressure improved with sublingual nitroglycerin as did 
his blood pressure.  He had no subsequent episodes of chest 
pressure and then developed an episode of nausea which resolved 
with zofran and compazine.  He then did well and had no 
subsequent complaints.  For his chest pressure, an EKG was 
checked which was unchanged and serial cardiac enzymes were 
checked and they were all negative.  On hospital day #3, he felt 
totally back to his usual state of health and requested 
discharge home.    
.

above, he tolerated it well though had some complaints on HD #2.
